Date : 10/07/2024  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

By way of the present application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23986/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2024 undefined short,
the 'Code'), the applicants pray for quashing and setting aside the FIR being C.R. No. I-113/2019 registered with Meghaninagar Police Station, Ahmedabad City for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code ("IPC" for short) and under Sections 3 and 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Heard learned advocate, Mr. Vijal Desai for the applicants and learned APP Mr. Soaham Joshi for respondent no.1.
Though served, the respondent no.2 has chosen not to appear.

3. Learned advocate submitted that the impugned FIR is filed by the complainant (wife) against four accused persons i.e. the husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law and out of them,
except the husband (the accused no.1), other accused have approached this Court by filing present quashing petition, wherein while admitting the matter, interim relief was granted, whereby further proceedings in connection with the impugned FIR have been stayed.

Learned advocate submitted that as stated above, except husband (the original accused no.1), other accused have approached and against the accused no.1, the investigation was carried out and at the end of investigation, the chargesheet was filed and, thereafter, the trial was proceeded further and at the end of trial, the learned Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court No.13, Ahmedabad, by an order dated 17.10.2022, acquitted the accused NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23986/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2024 undefined no.1, simple copy of which is produced on record.

entities.text: Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court No.13, Ahmedabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned advocate submitted that if the Hon'ble Court would make a cursory glance upon the said order, in that event,
it would be found out that the evidence of the complainant was recorded, wherein she has not supported the case of the prosecution and has been declared hostile and, thereafter as stated above,
an order of acquittal has been passed.
4. Learned advocate further submitted that in fact, pending this application, the respondent no.2 - wife had also instituted other proceedings before the court/ authority concerned i.e. the proceeding under the Hindu Marriage Act as well as under the Domestic Violence Act, however, those proceedings were disposed of on the strength of the settlement arrived at between the parties,
simple copies of those orders are placed on record in support of his submissions.

Learned advocate further submitted that thereafter, the husband and wife both have jointly filed Hindu Marriage Petition for mutual consent, which was eventually allowed by the concerned learned Family Judge and, thereafter, they have separated and are living happily in their respective life.

Learned advocate,
therefore, submitted that considering the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, reported in AIR 1992 SC 604 as well as in case of R.P.
Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, reported in AIR NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23986/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2024 undefined 1960 SC 866 : 1960 Cri LJ 1239, the present application may be allowed and the impugned FIR may be quashed and set aside as the same is sheer abuse of the process of law.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned APP Mr. Joshi has objected the present application and submitted that from the contents of the FIR, prima facie ingredients of the alleged offences are clearly spelt out from the body of the FIR.
It is, therefore, urged that the present application may not be entertained.

6. Having considered the submissions canvassed by learned advocates appearing for the parties and having gone through the material available, it is found out that the impugned FIR filed by the respondent no.2 - wife appears to be a matrimonial dispute between the husband and wife but as usual, all other family members have been roped in as accused persons.

It is also found out from the record that the accused no.1, who is husband, has not approached this Court and against him, the investigation was proceeded further and on conclusion of the same, the chargesheet was filed and after submission of the chargesheet, the trial was proceeded further and at the end of trial, an order of acquittal has been passed, copy of said order is produced on record.

On consideration of the observations made by the court concerned while passing an order of acquittal, it is found out that the respondent no.2 - wife was examined by NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23986/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2024 undefined the prosecution and she has not supported the case of the prosecution and has been turned hostile.

Further as stated above by learned advocate for the applicants that pending this application, other proceedings were also instituted by the respondent wife but subsequent on the strength of the settlement arrived at between the parties, the same were disposed of and/or withdrawn, copies of such orders are produced on record.
Over and above that on careful examination of the contents of the FIR, it do not disclose the commission of crime as alleged and same do not constitute any offence.

Thus from the above facts, it is found out that proceeding qua the accused no.1 (husband) is already concluded and settlement has taken place in other proceedings and, hence keeping the proceeding alive qua other family members would not serve any purpose and it would be considered to be futile exercise and wastage of precious time of the court.
Therefore, the present application deserves to be allowed.
7. I have also considered the the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, reported in AIR 1992 SC 604.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, reported in AIR 1992 SC 604
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court in the said judgment in case of Bhajan Lal (supra) has issued certain guidelines, which are required to be taken into consideration at the time of deciding quashing petition.

entities.text: Rakeshbhai Vrajvashi vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus in view of the broad guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid decision,
which have been followed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in subsequent decisions as well as by this Court from time to time and since now the dispute between the husband and wife is resolved as stated above, the continuation of proceedings would be futile exercise and any further continuation of proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.
Therefore, the impugned FIR is required to be quashed and set aside.
9. Resultantly, this application is allowed.

The impugned FIR being C.R. No. I-113/2019 registered with Meghaninagar Police Station, Ahmedabad and all other consequential proceedings arising out of said FIR are hereby quashed and set aside qua the applicants.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
